text.p: Azerbaijan's parliament on Friday approved a $758 million budget for 1997 which includes a $163 million deficit, a significant increase over 1996.

The Milli Mejlis, or parliament, approved spending of 3.18 trillion manats and revenues of 2.5 trillion manats. The 680 billion manat deficit is significantly more than in 1996 which it was 516 billion manats ($117 million at the then exchange rate).
The deficit is to be covered mainly by issuing treasury bills and "bonuses" paid into state coffers by western oil companies signing new offshore Caspian Sea drilling contracts with the government.
The government expects gross domestic product to rise two percent over 1996 levels to 17.2 trillion manats.
Education accounts for 648 billion manats, the biggest slice of government spending, while 357 billion go to defence, 278 billion for social security and 250 billion for health care.
Servicing the government debt will take 413 billion manats.

Some Milli Mejlis deputies complained about what they see as the relatively low level of military spending at a time when the country is still in conflict with neighbouring Armenia over the disputed territory of Nagorno-Karabakh.
Finance Minister Fikret Usifov said the government had collected nearly 100 percent of expected tax revenues for 1996.
($1 US = 4250 manat) -- Lawrence Sheets, Tbilisi bureau (995-32) 99-93-70
